about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

accommodation.en: a place to live or stay
accommodation.ex: The college offers accommodation to first-year students.

according.ex: According to the report, prices fell last year.

acknowledged.ex: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.

act.en: to do something to deal with a problem
act.ex: The council must act before the bridge collapses.

activity.en: something people do, often for fun
activity.ex: Swimming is my favourite weekend activity.

acute.ex: The hospital faces an acute shortage of nurses.

additional.ex: The school hired two additional teachers.

addressing.ex: The mayor was addressing a crowd of local residents.

ahead.ex: Ahead of the exam, she studied every night.

allocated.ex: The council allocated money for new parks.

alterations.ex: They made small alterations to the original plan.

ambitions.en: big goals or plans someone wants to achieve
ambitions.ex: Her ambitions include running her own company.

amid.en: during or surrounded by a situation

amount.ex: He paid the full amount in cash.

annual.en: every year (annual leave: holiday from work)
annual.ex: Workers get twenty days of annual leave.

annually.ex: The festival is held annually in May.

approaching.ex: The plane is approaching the airport now.

approximately.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.

argued.en: gave reasons to show something is true
argued.ex: He argued that the plan was too expensive.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asked.ex: She asked her boss for a day off.

asserted.ex: She asserted that the report was wrong.

association.en: an organisation of people or groups
association.ex: He joined the local football association.

at.es: a (at the same rate: al mismo ritmo)
at.hi: पर (at the same rate: उसी दर पर)
at.ja: 〜で（at the same rate：同じ割合で）
at.zh: 以（at the same rate：以相同速度）

authority.ex: The local authority closed the road.

backing.ex: The plan has the backing of local shops.

becoming.ex: The city is becoming more crowded every year.

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

before.ex: I had seen him two days before.

better.ex: Her temper got the better of her.
better.zh: get the better of：（好奇心）占了上風

board.en: a group that controls an organisation
board.ex: The board will vote on the new budget.

boosts.ex: A good night's sleep boosts your energy.

breaking.en: breaking point: the moment you cannot cope
breaking.ex: After weeks of overtime, the staff reached breaking point.

budget.ex: The government announced its budget on Tuesday.

build.ex: They plan to build a new school here.

business.en: the work of buying, selling or producing
business.ex: She runs a small business in Galway.

calling.ex: They are calling off the match because of rain.

campus.en: the land and buildings of a university
campus.ex: Most first-year students live on campus.

cannot.ex: You cannot park here after six.

capacity.en: the amount something can hold or supply
capacity.ex: The stadium has a capacity of 50,000 people.

chairman.en: the person who leads a board or meeting
chairman.ex: The chairman opened the meeting at nine.

chairs.en: leads a committee or meeting as its chair
chairs.ex: She chairs the school parents’ committee.

changes.ex: The new law brought many changes.

chronic.en: lasting a long time and hard to fix
chronic.ex: The town has a chronic lack of affordable homes.

example.en: The region suffers from a chronic lack of doctors.
example.zh: 這個地區長期缺乏醫生。

note.meaning: 長期存在、難以解決的（問題）；也指慢性的（疾病）。
note.usage: 多修飾負面名詞，如 shortage、underfunding、pain；強調問題長期持續，而非突然發生。

noteEn.meaning: Lasting for a long time and difficult to fix.
noteEn.usage: Used with problems like shortage or underfunding to show they never go away.

noteEs.exampleTr: La región sufre una falta crónica de médicos.
noteEs.meaning: Que dura mucho tiempo y es difícil de resolver; también enfermedad crónica.
noteEs.usage: Suele acompañar a sustantivos negativos como shortage o underfunding; subraya la persistencia del problema.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह क्षेत्र लंबे समय से डॉक्टरों की कमी से जूझ रहा है।
noteHi.meaning: लंबे समय से चली आ रही (समस्या); पुरानी बीमारी के लिए भी।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर shortage, underfunding जैसे नकारात्मक शब्दों के साथ; समस्या के लंबे समय तक बने रहने पर ज़ोर देता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その地域は慢性的な医師不足に苦しんでいる。
noteJa.meaning: 長く続き、解決が難しい（問題）。慢性の病気にも使う。
noteJa.usage: shortage や underfunding など否定的な名詞と結びつき、問題の長期性を強調する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 지역은 만성적인 의사 부족에 시달린다.
noteKo.meaning: 오래 지속되어 해결하기 어려운 (문제); 만성 질환에도 쓴다.
noteKo.usage: shortage, underfunding 같은 부정적 명사와 자주 쓰이며 문제의 장기성을 강조한다.

cliff.en: a high steep rock edge; here, danger
cliff.ex: We walked carefully along the top of the cliff.

closed.en: made smaller until it disappears (a gap)
closed.ex: The team closed the gap with a late goal.

coincide.en: to happen at the same time
coincide.ex: The festival will coincide with the school holidays.

example.en: The concert will coincide with the city festival.
example.zh: 這場音樂會將與城市節慶同時舉行。

note.usage: 常用 coincide with + 事件；主詞是事件或時間，不是人。

noteEn.meaning: To happen at the same time as something else.
noteEn.usage: Use "coincide with"; the subject is an event, not a person.

noteEs.exampleTr: El concierto coincidirá con el festival de la ciudad.
noteEs.usage: Se usa coincide with + evento; el sujeto es un hecho, no una persona.

noteHi.exampleTr: संगीत कार्यक्रम शहर के उत्सव के साथ ही होगा।
noteHi.usage: coincide with + घटना; कर्ता घटना या समय होता है, व्यक्ति नहीं।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのコンサートは市の祭りと同時に開かれる。
noteJa.usage: coincide with + 出来事の形で、主語は人ではなく出来事や時期。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 콘서트는 시 축제와 동시에 열린다.
noteKo.usage: coincide with + 사건 형태로 쓰며, 주어는 사람이 아닌 사건이나 시기다.

college.ex: She studies history at a local college.
college.ja: カレッジ（Trinity College：トリニティ・カレッジ）
college.zh: 學院（Trinity College：都柏林三一學院）

come.ex: Most of our food comes from abroad.

comes.en: arrives (comes from: has its origin in)
comes.ex: Most of our coffee comes from Brazil.

commercial.ex: The land is used for commercial farming.

committee.en: a group chosen to do a task
committee.ex: The committee will decide next week.

commute.en: to travel regularly to school or work
commute.ex: Many workers commute to the city by train.

commutes.en: regular trips to school or work
commutes.ex: Her daily commute takes over an hour.

commuting.en: travelling regularly between home and school
commuting.ex: He spends two hours commuting every day.

compounded.ex: The flood damage was compounded by heavy winds.

example.en: Bad weather compounded the traffic problems.
example.zh: 惡劣天氣使交通問題雪上加霜。

note.usage: 多用被動 be compounded by；受詞通常是 problem、difficulty 等負面名詞。

noteEn.meaning: To make a bad problem even worse.

noteEs.exampleTr: El mal tiempo agravó los problemas de tráfico.
noteEs.usage: Muy común en pasiva be compounded by; con problem, difficulty, etc.

noteHi.exampleTr: खराब मौसम ने यातायात की समस्याओं को और बढ़ा दिया।
noteHi.meaning: (क्रिया) समस्या को और बढ़ाना या बदतर बनाना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर कर्मवाच्य be compounded by; problem, difficulty जैसे शब्दों के साथ।

noteJa.exampleTr: 悪天候が交通問題をさらに悪化させた。
noteJa.meaning: （動詞）問題をさらに悪化させる。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be compounded by が多く、problem や difficulty など否定的な語と使う。

noteKo.usage: 수동태 be compounded by가 흔하며 problem, difficulty 같은 부정적 명사와 쓴다.

consequence.ex: He lost his job as a consequence of the accident.
consequence.zh: as a consequence of：由於…的結果

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerable.ex: The change saved a considerable amount of money.

construction.en: the building of houses or structures
construction.ex: Construction of the bridge began in May.

contain.ex: This drink does not contain sugar.

contended.ex: She contended that the test was unfair.

example.en: Experts contend that the plan will not work.
example.zh: 專家堅稱這項計畫行不通。

note.usage: contend that + 子句，用於正式論述；另有 contend with「應付（困難）」。

noteEn.meaning: To say firmly that something is true.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los expertos sostienen que el plan no funcionará.
noteEs.meaning: Sostener o afirmar algo con firmeza.
noteEs.usage: contend that + oración, en registro formal; contend with significa "lidiar con".

noteHi.exampleTr: विशेषज्ञों का दावा है कि यह योजना काम नहीं करेगी।
noteHi.meaning: ज़ोर देकर दावा करना कि कुछ सच है।
noteHi.usage: contend that + वाक्य, औपचारिक तर्क में; contend with का अर्थ "कठिनाई से निपटना"।

noteJa.exampleTr: 専門家たちはその計画はうまくいかないと主張している。
noteJa.usage: contend that + 節で改まった議論に使う。contend with は「（困難に）対処する」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 전문가들은 그 계획이 효과가 없을 것이라고 주장한다.
noteKo.usage: contend that + 절로 격식 있는 논의에 쓰며, contend with는 "(어려움에) 대처하다".

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent on government funding.

example.en: The trip is contingent on good weather.
example.zh: 這趟旅行能否成行取決於天氣好壞。

note.usage: 固定搭配 contingent on/upon；正式用語，類似 depending on。

noteEs.exampleTr: El viaje depende del buen tiempo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa contingent on/upon; registro formal, similar a depending on.

noteHi.exampleTr: यात्रा अच्छे मौसम पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.usage: contingent on/upon के रूप में; औपचारिक, depending on जैसा।

noteJa.exampleTr: その旅行は天気次第だ。
noteJa.usage: contingent on / upon の形で使う改まった表現。depending on に近い。

noteKo.usage: contingent on/upon 형태로 쓰는 격식 표현으로 depending on과 비슷하다.

contribution.en: money paid as a share of a cost
contribution.ex: Each member makes a monthly contribution to the fund.

cork's.en: belonging to Cork, a city in Ireland

cost.en: to need an amount of money; price

costs.ex: The cost of living keeps rising.

couch-surf.en: to sleep on friends’ sofas for free
couch-surf.ex: After losing his flat, he had to couch-surf for months.
couch-surf.ja: 人の家のソファを転々とする

couch-surfing.ex: She was couch-surfing while she looked for a room.
couch-surfing.hi: दूसरों के सोफे पर सोते हुए
couch-surfing.ja: ソファを転々とすること

countries.ex: Ireland is a small country with a big diaspora.

crisis.ex: The country faced an economic crisis.

current.ex: The current rules are too strict.

day.ex: It was a long day at work.

debate.en: a discussion where people give opinions
debate.ex: There was a long debate about school fees.

decade.ex: Prices have doubled in a decade.

deficit.en: money spent above what you have
deficit.ex: The company has a large deficit.

dependent.ex: The town is dependent on tourism.

deprive.en: to take something away from someone
deprive.ex: The new rules could deprive farmers of their income.

example.en: The strike deprived thousands of people of transport.
example.zh: 罷工讓數千人無法搭乘交通工具。

note.usage: 句型 deprive + 人/機構 + of + 事物；被動 be deprived of。

noteEn.meaning: To take away something that someone needs.

noteEs.exampleTr: La huelga privó de transporte a miles de personas.
noteEs.meaning: Privar a alguien de algo que necesita o merece.
noteEs.usage: Estructura deprive + persona + of + cosa; pasiva be deprived of.

noteHi.exampleTr: हड़ताल ने हज़ारों लोगों को परिवहन से वंचित कर दिया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी से कोई ज़रूरी चीज़ छीन लेना।
noteHi.usage: deprive + व्यक्ति + of + वस्तु; कर्मवाच्य be deprived of।

noteJa.exampleTr: ストライキで何千人もの人が交通手段を奪われた。
noteJa.usage: deprive + 人 / 組織 + of + 物の形。受動態は be deprived of。

noteKo.usage: deprive + 사람/기관 + of + 대상 구조이며, 수동태는 be deprived of.

deterring.en: making people not want to do something
deterring.ex: High prices are deterring tourists from visiting.

did.ex: Our team did well in the final.

director.en: the person in charge of an organisation
director.ex: The director announced new plans for the company.

distances.ex: They walked long distances to find water.

do.en: used instead of repeating a verb
do.ex: I like tea, and my sister does too.

does.ex: He does his homework after dinner.
does.zh: 做；進行（does a survey：做調查）

drastically.en: very much and in a serious way
drastically.ex: Prices fell drastically after the holiday season.

earmarking.en: setting money aside for a purpose
earmarking.ex: The council is earmarking funds for a new park.

example.en: The city has earmarked €5 million for new bike lanes.
example.zh: 市政府已撥出五百萬歐元興建新自行車道。

note.meaning: 指定（款項）作特定用途；撥出。
note.usage: 常用 earmark + 金額 + for + 用途，或被動 be earmarked for。

noteEn.meaning: To set money aside for a particular purpose.
noteEn.usage: Use "earmark money for something" or "be earmarked for".

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad ha destinado 5 millones de euros a nuevos carriles bici.
noteEs.meaning: Destinar dinero a un fin concreto.
noteEs.usage: Se usa earmark + cantidad + for + fin, o en pasiva be earmarked for.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर ने नई साइकिल लेन के लिए €50 लाख निर्धारित किए हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी खास काम के लिए धन निर्धारित करना।
noteHi.usage: earmark + राशि + for + उद्देश्य या be earmarked for के रूप में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市は新しい自転車レーンに500万ユーロを充てた。
noteJa.meaning: （資金を）特定の目的に充てる、割り当てる。
noteJa.usage: earmark + 金額 + for + 用途、または受動態 be earmarked for で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시는 새 자전거 도로에 500만 유로를 배정했다.
noteKo.usage: earmark + 금액 + for + 용도, 또는 수동태 be earmarked for로 쓴다.

edge.ex: Do not stand too close to the edge.

education.ex: Higher education is free for some students.

eliminate.ex: We want to eliminate waste in the office.

enduring.en: suffering something difficult for a long time
enduring.ex: The villagers are enduring a long, cold winter.

enrolment.en: the number of students joining a course
enrolment.ex: Enrolment at the college rose by ten percent.

essentially.en: basically; in the most important way
essentially.ex: The two phones are essentially the same.

estimated.en: guessed the size or cost of
estimated.ex: Experts estimated the damage at €2 million.

ever.en: ever more: more and more over time

evidence.en: something that shows a thing is true
evidence.ex: The new jobs are evidence that the town is growing.

excessive.ex: Excessive screen time can harm your sleep.

existing.ex: We will improve the existing system.

extra.ex: The job comes with extra holidays.

facilitate.en: to make something easier to happen
facilitate.ex: The new app will facilitate online bookings.

example.zh: 良好的照明有助於閱讀。

note.usage: 受詞是過程或活動（facilitate learning / the construction of）；主詞通常是事物或機構，不接人當受詞。

noteEn.meaning: To make a process or action easier.
noteEn.usage: The object is an activity, e.g. "facilitate learning".

noteEs.exampleTr: Una buena iluminación puede facilitar la lectura.
noteEs.meaning: Facilitar; hacer que algo sea más fácil.
noteEs.usage: El objeto es un proceso o actividad (facilitate learning), no una persona.

noteHi.exampleTr: अच्छी रोशनी पढ़ने को आसान बना सकती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी काम को आसान बनाना या बढ़ावा देना।
noteHi.usage: कर्म कोई प्रक्रिया होती है (facilitate learning); व्यक्ति कर्म नहीं होता।

noteJa.exampleTr: 良い照明は読書をしやすくする。
noteJa.meaning: 促進する、〜を容易にする。
noteJa.usage: 目的語は過程や活動（facilitate learning など）で、人を目的語にしない。

noteKo.exampleTr: 좋은 조명은 독서를 쉽게 해 준다.
noteKo.usage: 목적어는 과정이나 활동(facilitate learning 등)이며 사람을 목적어로 쓰지 않는다.

failed.ex: The talks failed to produce a deal.

families.ex: She lives with her family in Cork.

far.ex: This is far better than the old version.
far.ja: はるかに（far from：決して〜ない）
syn: a lot (far from: not at all)

fared.en: did or got on in a situation
fared.ex: How did you fare in the job interview?

fee.ex: There is a small fee to enter.

fees.ex: School fees went up this year.

figure.ex: The official figure is much higher.

financially.ex: The shop is not financially stable yet.

find.en: to discover or get something you need
find.ex: I cannot find my keys anywhere.

fraction.en: a very small part of something
fraction.ex: He sold the house for a fraction of its value.

friends.en: people you know and like (in a book title)
friends.ex: I met my friends at the park.
friends.zh: 朋友（書名 Conversations with Friends）

gap.ex: There is a gap in the budget.

gave.ex: Her parents gave her a bike for her birthday.

general.en: normal, not for a special type
general.ex: Put the paper in the general recycling box.
general.zh: 一般的（general bin：一般垃圾桶）

gifts.ex: The museum depends on gifts from the public.

given.ex: Given the rain, we stayed inside.

gives.ex: The plan gives more money to schools.

go.en: go down/up: become lower or higher
go.ex: Bus fares will go up next month.

governing.ex: The governing body meets once a month.

government.en: the group that runs a country

grants.en: money given for a purpose, not repaid
grants.ex: She received a grant to study abroad.

greater.ex: The plan needs greater support from parents.

group.en: a number of people or things together
group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

had.en: possessed; was involved (had a hand in)
had.ex: She had a key role in the project.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

head.ex: She is the head of the science department.

heard.ex: The court heard evidence from three witnesses.

help.ex: Volunteers help older people with shopping.

homes.ex: Many students rent a room in a family home.

housing.en: homes for people to live in
housing.ex: The city needs more cheap housing.

however.ex: It was sunny; however, it was cold.

important.ex: It is important to drink water.

income.ex: Rent takes half of her income.

increasing.ex: There was a sharp increase in prices.

insist.en: to say firmly that something is true
insist.ex: They insist that the plan will work.

institution.en: a large organisation such as a university
institution.ex: Oxford is one of the oldest institutions in Europe.

institutions.ja: 機関（higher education institutions：高等教育機関）
institutions.zh: 機構（higher education institutions：大專院校）

insufficiently.ex: The room was insufficiently heated in winter.

international.ex: She works for an international charity.

investment.en: money put in to get results

issue.ex: Housing is a major issue for young people.

juggling.en: trying to manage several things at once
juggling.ex: She is juggling two jobs and a family.

just.ex: Just over half the class passed.

key.ex: Trust is a key part of any friendship.

left.en: caused someone to be in a situation
left.ex: The storm left thousands without power.

lengthy.ex: After a lengthy delay, the train finally left.

less.ex: I spend less on food now.

level.en: an amount or height on a scale
level.ex: The level of debt is too high.

lie.en: to be in a certain position or situation
lie.ex: The answer may lie in better planning.

limit.ex: My patience has reached its limit.

linked.ex: Poor sleep is linked to stress.

live.ex: They live in a small town.

living.en: cost of living: money needed for daily life
living.ex: The cost of living in big cities is high.

loss.ex: The loss of forests harms wildlife.

maintained.ex: He maintains that the plan will work.

maintenance.en: money to pay for living costs
maintenance.ex: Students can apply for a maintenance grant.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

markets.en: places where people buy and sell
markets.ex: We buy fish at the Saturday market.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

measures.en: finds the size or amount of something
measures.ex: This test measures your reading speed.

mere.ex: The tickets sold out in a mere ten minutes.

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

missing.en: not having something that is needed
missing.ex: The team is missing two key players.

money.ex: They saved money for a new car.

moving.ex: The police are moving quickly on the case.

national.ex: The national team won the match.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

new.ex: The city opened a new library.

non-exchequer.ex: The library raised non-Exchequer funds from local firms.
non-exchequer.zh: 非國庫的（非政府撥款的）

notably.ex: Notably, sales rose during the winter.

now.ex: The shop is now open on Sundays.

objectives.ex: The project has three main objectives.

obliged.ex: Drivers are obliged to wear seat belts.

observed.ex: She observed that the room was very quiet.

on.en: used in 'pass on' = give to someone else
on.ex: Please pass the message on to your sister.

on-campus.ex: The on-campus gym is free for students.

other.ex: She moved to another city to find other work.

outside.en: not from or part of something

overseas.en: from or in a foreign country
overseas.ex: The school welcomes many overseas students.

package.en: a set of measures offered together
package.ex: The government announced an aid package for farmers.

paid.ex: She found paid work during the summer.

pay.ex: I will pay for dinner tonight.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

per-student.ex: Per-student spending has fallen in many schools.

period.ex: The museum is closed for a short period.

paragraphs: Irish universities say they need more money. Their leaders spoke to a group of politicians on Thursday. They said the universities are close to a "cliff edge".
The universities say they are short of about €250 million every year. The State now gives 34% less money for each student than in 2008.
The universities asked for €190 million more. The new budget gives them only €10 million.
The budget does help students. Fees will go down by €150. Grants for students will go up by 4.5%.
University College Cork says new visa rules will cost it €3.7 million. Fewer students may come from other countries.
Many students also cannot find a place to live. Some travel very far to college every day. The universities want help to build more rooms for students.
Irish universities are close to a "cliff edge" because the State has not given them enough money for many years. University leaders told this to the Oireachtas education committee on Thursday.

Paul Johnson, the head of the Irish Universities Association, said the sector is missing about €250 million every year. He said the Government understands the problem but is not moving fast enough. Today the State spends 34% less on each student than it did in 2008.
Before the budget, the universities asked for an extra €190 million over this year and next year. But Budget 2027 gave them only €10 million in new core funding.

The budget did include a €34 million package for students. The student fee will fall by €150, and SUSI grants, which help students pay for living costs, will rise by 4.5%. Paul Farrell of Trinity College Dublin welcomed this help but said universities are only "treading water". Mike Beary of UCD said the universities are already full and cannot do more with the money they have.

University College Cork now depends more on money from other places, such as gifts, overseas students and business. Its chairman, Sean O'Driscoll, said changes to visa rules will cost the college €3.7 million in 2026/27, because fewer students may come from important countries.

The problem is linked to a housing crisis for students. Many travel long distances, sleep on friends' sofas or work long hours. The universities want the State to close the funding gap and to help them build more homes for students on campus.
Irish universities are standing on a "cliff edge" after years of chronic underfunding by the State, the Oireachtas education committee heard on Thursday.

Paul Johnson, director general of the Irish Universities Association, told TDs and senators that the sector faces a funding gap of around €250 million a year. He said the Government had acknowledged the problem but had failed to act quickly enough. State funding per student is now 34% lower than it was in 2008.
In their pre-budget submission, the universities requested an additional €190 million in core funding over this year and next. Budget 2027, however, allocated just €10 million in new core funding.

The budget did contain a €34 million support package for students, cutting the student contribution fee by €150 and increasing SUSI maintenance grants by 4.5%. Paul Farrell, chairman of Trinity College Dublin's board, welcomed these measures but warned that universities were merely "treading water". Mike Beary, who chairs UCD's governing authority, said the sector had reached the limit of its capacity.

Sean O'Driscoll, chairman of University College Cork's governing authority, said the college increasingly relies on income from outside the Exchequer, such as philanthropy, international students and commercial activity. He estimated that recent changes to visa policy would cost UCC €3.7 million in 2026/27 by reducing recruitment from key overseas markets.

The debate comes amid a worsening student accommodation crisis, with many students commuting long distances, couch-surfing or working long hours. The universities are calling on the State to close the core funding gap and to provide more support for on-campus housing, which they say is not financially viable on their own.
Ireland's universities are teetering on a "cliff edge" after more than a decade of chronic underinvestment by the State, an Oireachtas committee was told on Thursday.

Addressing the education committee, Paul Johnson, director general of the Irish Universities Association, put the sector's annual funding shortfall at roughly €250 million. While the Government had recognised the scale of the problem, he argued, it had been far too slow to remedy it. Per-student State funding remains 34% below its 2008 level.
Ahead of the budget, the universities had sought an extra €190 million in core funding spread over two years. Budget 2027 fell drastically short, earmarking a mere €10 million.

Students fared somewhat better, with a €34 million package that trims the student contribution fee by €150 and boosts SUSI maintenance grants by 4.5%. Paul Farrell, who chairs Trinity College Dublin's board, welcomed the relief for families but cautioned that institutions were simply "treading water". Mike Beary of UCD contended that the sector was stretched to breaking point and could not underpin the country's economic and social ambitions with its existing resources.

Sean O'Driscoll of University College Cork said the institution was becoming ever more reliant on non-Exchequer income, from philanthropy to overseas recruitment and commercial ventures. He estimated that recent visa changes, which lie beyond the sector's control, would deprive UCC of €3.7 million in 2026/27 by deterring students from key markets.

The warnings coincide with an acute shortage of student accommodation, which has left many students enduring lengthy commutes, couch-surfing or juggling long hours of paid work. The universities want the funding gap closed and greater State backing for on-campus housing, which they insist is unviable without public support.

Paul Johnson, director general of the Irish Universities Association, estimated that the sector faces a substantial funding deficit of approximately €250 million annually. Although the Government has acknowledged the issue, he maintained that its response has been insufficiently prompt. Notably, State expenditure per student remains 34% lower than in 2008.

Prior to the budget, the universities had requested an additional €190 million in core funding over a two-year period. Nevertheless, Budget 2027 allocated only €10 million, a figure that represents a mere fraction of the amount sought.

The budget did, however, incorporate a €34 million package of student supports, reducing the student contribution fee by €150 and raising SUSI maintenance grants by 4.5%.
